sections.h2: Who does what with property tax
sections.html:
Three parties touch an Outagamie County tax bill. Your municipal assessor sets the value in your city, village or town. The county Property Listing Office keeps ownership, legal descriptions, lottery credits and assessment records, and it prepares the assessment roll, notices and bills. The Outagamie County Treasurer, at 320 S. Walnut Street in Appleton, receipts second installments and delinquent payments. Call the treasurer at (920) 832-5065.

Collection follows Chapter 74 of the Wisconsin Statutes. If a lender escrows your taxes, the bill still arrives at your mailing address, and you must sort out timing with the lender, because bills can't be mailed to a mortgage loan or escrow agent.

sections.h2: Due dates and who gets the payment
sections.html:
Your local municipal treasurer gets the full payment, or the first half, on or before January 31. The county treasurer can take the July 31 second half and anything delinquent. Each stub across the top of the bill states the amount, the date and where it goes.

Appleton works differently. Owners of Appleton parcels pay current taxes to the city, and the county sends them to the city website and (920) 832-6442. Every other municipality offers the two-installment choice.

The schedule rests on Wis. Stat. 74.11: two equal halves, and one lump sum by January 31 if the parcel's tax is below $100.

Options are online, phone, mail, deposit box or in person. The online system asks for the nine-digit parcel number, since the first three digits on a bill are administrative only. The county posts a property tax payment guide as well.

Payment methodFee or detail
Online by e-check$1.50
Online by debit card$3.50
Online by credit card2.5% of the payment
Phone (920) 832-5065Confirm payoff amounts and pay by phone
Mail to 320 S. Walnut Street, Appleton, WI 54911Receipted by postmark date; include a stamped envelope for a receipt
Deposit box, Door #1For second installment or delinquent payments

The counter is at the same address. Use the public entrance at Door #1 and pass through security first.

A payment isn't delinquent if it arrives within five working days of the January 31 or July 31 due date. As the county's example, a July 31 due date carries a grace date of August 7, and it takes walk-in payments through August 7 and mailed ones received by then (Wis. Stat. 74.11(7) and 74.12(7)).

Once the grace period ends, the penalties are real:

  • A first payment after January 31, or a second installment after July 31, makes the taxes delinquent and the whole amount due, whether you were paying in full or by installment.
  • Interest of one percent per month accrues on the unpaid balance from February 1 (Wis. Stat. 74.47(1)).
  • For delinquent real estate taxes the county offers monthly automatic deduction under a notarized payment agreement. Deductions happen on the 10th or 25th, and changes must reach the office by the 5th or 20th at (920) 832-5065.

A delinquent tax report is also posted for anyone to download. Before you list, check whether your parcel appears on it, because a buyer's title company will run the same check and an unexpected balance can delay closing.

The county seat runs its own collection. Owners can walk into City Hall (100 N. Appleton St.) and use the first floor service desk, drive-up window, night deposit box or lobby drop box, or they can mail P.O. Box 2519, Appleton, WI 54912-2519, or go online. The counter and drive-up are staffed 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, holidays excepted.

Four installments are offered here: January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. One late payment cancels the installment option and starts monthly interest from February 1, per state law. Balances still owed on 2025 and earlier bills are delinquent and go to the treasurer of whichever county holds the parcel. Outagamie is (920) 832-5065, Calumet (920) 849-1457 and Winnebago (920) 232-3420.

Your local assessor is the first call. Property Listing Office staff refer assessment questions and disputes there and point to the Wisconsin Municipal Assessors List. You can view your record on the county's Ascent Land Records site, searching by parcel ID, address or name.

Not resolved? Take it to the board of review in your municipality. Wis. Stat. 70.47 wants notice to the clerk, written or spoken, 48 hours or more before the opening meeting, and a written objection filed during the first two hours of that meeting, though good cause can excuse the notice. The municipal clerk supplies the date and the form.

Earlier assessment and tax rolls sit on the county Open Data site, and the current year's rolls go up in January of the next year.

Wisconsin residents can claim the lottery and gaming credit on a primary residence held on January 1. It excludes rentals, business property, vacant land and garages, and a person gets one residence. Owners must ask for it. Find it missing on your bill? Apply to the municipal treasurer by January 31 after the bill arrives, or submit a late claim to the Department of Revenue by October 1.

Because the Property Listing Office maintains these credits, the Real Property Lister at 920-832-5665 can answer questions about your parcel.

sections.h2: Selling a house with taxes owed
sections.html:
First, figure out which office is owed what. Appleton sellers owe the city current taxes and the county any delinquent amount. Elsewhere, the local treasurer takes the first installment and the county can receipt the second.

  • Request a payoff from the treasurer ahead of closing, since one percent a month builds from February 1.
  • Confirm the owner name and mailing address on file. Ascent Land Records takes address change requests, and an update can take up to 24 hours to show.
  • A lottery credit follows the parcel, so ask how your contract splits the bill.
  • Have the closing agent deduct any delinquent taxes from your proceeds.

With a cash buyer, the closing agent can often send the payoff straight to the treasurer within days, so an overdue balance needn't stall the sale.

Population reached an estimated 195,894 on July 1, 2025, a 2.7 percent rise over 190,700 in 2020. About 71.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied, valued at a median of $267,300, while median gross rent is $1,057. Housing units number 82,646 across 78,382 households, and 1,022 building permits were issued in 2025.

faqs.a: January 31 for the first installment or full payment, July 31 for the second. Your local municipal treasurer gets the first, and the county treasurer can receipt the second plus delinquent payments.

The City of Appleton takes current taxes at City Hall, 100 N. Appleton St., by mail or online, in four installments (January 31, March 31, May 31, July 31). Delinquent balances move to the county treasurer.
Yes, five working days past January 31 or July 31. The county's July example ends August 7, and after that the balance is delinquent and accrues one percent monthly.
Interest of one percent monthly on what's unpaid, counted from February 1 (Wis. Stat. 74.47(1)). Paying any installment late puts the rest of the tax due at once.

The county treasurer, (920) 832-5065, handles payments and payoffs. For owner or property record questions, try the Real Property Lister, 920-832-5665. Appleton parcels go through the city at (920) 832-6442.
